name: JumpLink
description: Single in-page anchor link: a ControlButton (media style, md) paired with a heading-5 label. JumpLinkNav arranges N JumpLinks in a row with a 32px gap. Used in rich-content sections to jump down to further sections on the same page.
composedOf: ControlButton (visual parity only — shares control-button.css, rendered as a non-interactive span so the whole JumpLink stays a single <a>, never a <button> nested inside a link)

figma.sourcePattern: Rich-content-jump-link-Desktop_Enhancement (13027:189213), CPro — Hub and docementation cleanup file

props.name: orientation
props.description: JumpLinkNav only (Figma VARIANT prop Orientation, component set 13371:188842) — matches the Orientation name/values/default already used by Card and ProductLockup

knownTokenGaps: --s2a-spacing-xs is bound in Figma (s2a/spacing/xs) but marked hiddenFromPublishing — not in shipped CSS output yet. CSS carries an 8px fallback until it ships.
--s2a-font-weight-heading resolves to the design-only --s2a-font-weight-adobe-clean-display-black in Figma; CSS uses the shipped semantic alias with a 900 fallback (same convention as Tabs).

notes: Renders as a native <a href="#section-id"> wrapping both the icon and the label — the whole item is one link target, not two separate controls.

The icon chip reuses ControlButton's CSS class for visual parity but is a non-interactive <span aria-hidden="true">, not a nested <button> — a <button> inside an <a> would be invalid, ambiguous-focus markup.
The link's accessible name comes entirely from the visible label text.
Focus ring is 1px focus-ring/default, same convention as Link and Tabs.
Color is not the only affordance — label text is always present alongside the icon (1.4.1).

Source composition (13027:189213) used the legacy ControlButton v1 (Context=on-media, Background=transparent) — JumpLink instead uses the current ControlButton v2 default variant (Style=media, Size=md, State=default), matching the already-shipped control-button code component.
JumpLinkNav is a fixed 3-item example composition per Orientation variant in Figma (mirrors the Tabs/TabGroup precedent); the code JumpLinkNav takes an array of {label, href} and renders N JumpLinks.

Orientation added as a Figma VARIANT prop (Title Case name, lowercase-kebab values, default horizontal) — same name/values/default as Card and ProductLockup, so orientation is a single system-wide concept rather than a per-component convention.

Vertical gap (--s2a-spacing-md, 16px) is tighter than the horizontal gap (--s2a-spacing-xl, 32px) — a deliberate choice (no source design to measure against) so a stacked list reads like a compact nav list rather than a spread-out row; mirrors ProductLockup's own horizontal/vertical gap tightening.
